items.title: Section: "Follow This, and You Are Called a Dharma King" — And a New Sutra Begins

items.zh: 復次，大王當知！我已略說王之過失、王之功德、王衰損門、王方便門、王可愛法，及能引發王可愛法，是故大王應當修學。王之過失宜當遠離，王之功德宜當修習，王衰損門宜當遠離，王方便門宜當修學，王可愛法宜當希慕，能引發王可愛之法宜當受行。大王若能如是修學，當獲一切利益安樂。復次，如說生苦，乃至略說五取蘊苦。
items.en: Moreover, Great King, you should know: I have now briefly explained a king's faults, a king's virtues, the gateways of a king's decline, the gateways of a king's skilful means, the qualities beloved of a king, and what draws forth those beloved qualities — therefore, Great King, you should diligently take up this practice. A king's faults should be distanced from; a king's virtues should be cultivated; the gateways of decline should be distanced from; the gateways of skilful means should be diligently practised; the qualities beloved of a king should be genuinely aspired to; and what draws forth those beloved qualities should be actually put into practice. Great King, if you can practise in this way, you will obtain every benefit and happiness. Moreover, as birth's suffering has been explained, so, in brief, is it reducible to the suffering of the five clinging-aggregates.

items.title: Section: Five Marks of the Suffering of Being Born at All

items.zh: 云何生苦？當知此苦由五種相。謂眾苦所隨故，麁重所隨故，眾苦所依故，煩惱所依故，不隨所欲離別法故。云何眾苦所隨故苦？謂生那落迦及一向苦餓鬼趣中，若於胎生、卵生生時，種種憂苦之所隨逐，故名眾苦所隨故苦。云何麁重所隨故苦？謂三界諸行，為煩惱品麁重所隨，性不調柔，不自在轉，由此隨逐三界有情諸行生起，故名麁重所隨故苦。云何眾苦所依故苦？謂衰老等眾苦差別之所依故。云何煩惱所依故苦？謂受生已，於愛境愛，於瞋境瞋，於癡境癡，由是因緣，住不寂靜惛蕩身心不安隱苦，故名煩惱所依故苦。云何不隨所欲離別法故苦？謂諸有情生者皆死、生必殞沒，所有壽命死為邊際、死為終極，如是等事非其所愛，由此因緣，唯受眾苦，是以不隨所欲離別法故，說生為苦。
items.en: What is birth's suffering? It should be known that this suffering has five marks: being accompanied by many sufferings, being accompanied by coarse-heaviness, being the basis of many sufferings, being the basis of affliction, and being the impossibility of avoiding an unwanted separation. What is the suffering of being accompanied by many sufferings? A being born in hell or in the uniformly painful hungry-ghost realm, whether through womb-birth or egg-birth, is followed from birth by manifold sorrow. What is the suffering of being the basis of many sufferings? Old age and its many differing sufferings all depend on birth. What is the suffering of being the basis of affliction? A being, once born, craves the agreeable, resents what provokes anger, and grows confused before confusion, and by this cause dwells in unsettled, disturbed, unsteady body and mind. What is the suffering of the impossibility of avoiding an unwanted separation? All beings that are born also die, death marking the very limit and end of life, an outcome unwelcome to any of them, and by this cause they experience nothing but suffering — it is for this reason, the impossibility of avoiding an unwanted parting, that birth itself is called suffering.

items.title: Section: A Lamp Whose Oil Is Nearly Spent

items.zh: 云何老苦？當知亦由五相。謂於五處衰退故苦。一、盛色衰退故；二、氣力衰退故；三、諸根衰退故；四、受用境界衰退故；五、壽量衰退故。云何病苦？當知病苦亦由五相。一、身性變壞故；二、憂苦增長多住故；三、於可意境不喜受用故；四、於不可意境非其所欲強受用故；五、能令命根速離壞故。云何死苦？當知此苦亦由五相。一、離別所愛盛財寶故；二、離別所愛盛朋友故；三、離別所愛盛眷屬故；
items.en: What is old age's suffering? It should be known that this too has five marks: the decline of one's radiant appearance, the decline of one's vigour, the decline of the sense faculties, the decline of one's capacity to enjoy sense objects, and the decline of one's own remaining lifespan. What is sickness's suffering? It should be known that this too has five marks: the body's own deterioration, the growth and prolonged dwelling of worry and distress, the inability to enjoy agreeable objects, being forced against one's own wish to endure disagreeable ones, and the hastening of the life-faculty's own dissolution. What is death's suffering? It should be known that this too has five marks: separation from one's own beloved, abundant wealth; separation from one's own beloved, cherished friends; separation from one's own beloved, cherished family.

items.title: Section: "One Comes Alone and Departs Alone" — Death, Hatred, and Separation

items.zh: 四、離別所愛盛自身故；五、於命終時備受種種極重憂苦故。云何怨憎會苦？當知此苦亦由五相。一、與彼會生憂苦故；二、治罰畏所依止故；三、惡名畏所依止故；四、苦逼迫命終怖畏所依止故；五、越正法惡趣怖畏所依止故。云何愛別離苦？當知此苦亦由五相。謂不與彼會生愁惱故，由此因緣生愁歎故，由此因緣身擾惱故，念彼眾德思戀因緣意熱惱故，應受用等有所闕故。
items.en: Fourth, separation from one's own beloved body. Fifth, enduring every kind of extreme distress at the time of death. What is the suffering of encountering what is hated? It should be known that this too has five marks: sorrow arising simply in that encounter; fear of retaliation and punishment; fear of slander; fear of death from that very oppression; and fear of falling into the evil destinies through conduct that transgresses the correct Dharma. What is the suffering of separation from what is loved? It should be known that this too has five marks: sorrow at not being together; resentment and lament arising from this cause; bodily distress arising from this cause; burning affliction of mind arising from longing for that being's own good qualities; and the loss of whatever mutual enjoyment ought to have continued.

items.title: Section: The Eighth Suffering — And a Deep Digression Into the Suffering of Formations Itself

items.zh: 如愛別離苦，求不得苦，當知亦爾。云何五取蘊苦？當知此苦亦由五相。謂生苦器故，依生苦器故，苦苦器故，壞苦器故，行苦性故。
items.en: As with the suffering of separation from what is loved, so too the suffering of not obtaining what is wanted. What is the suffering of the five clinging-aggregates? It should be known that this too has five marks: being the vessel of birth's suffering, being the vessel of the suffering that depends on birth, being the vessel of the suffering of pain, being the vessel of the suffering of change, and being, in nature, the suffering of formations. Moreover, as the Blessed One spoke of three kinds of suffering nature, what here is called the suffering of formations? Formations produced by karma that generates future existence and by affliction, within each and every embodied being, capable of giving rise to every affliction and every suffering in turn, established as belonging entirely to pervasive coarse-heaviness, also called coarse-heaviness, is the very nature of the suffering of formations. It is on the basis of this suffering of formations that the Blessed One said, in brief, that the five clinging-aggregates are all called suffering.

items.title: Section: Two Kinds of Cessation, and a Third Sutra on Three Kinds of Persons

items.zh: 復次，依行差別建立三士，謂下中上。無自利行無利他行，名為下士；有自利行無利他行，有利他行無自利行，名為中士；有自利行有利他行，名為上士。
items.en: Within the Blessed One's own sutras, based on the supreme principle, only craving is shown. Moreover, the permanent extinguishing of this affliction class's own coarse-heaviness is the truth of cessation established on the strength of nirvana with residue. Also, the permanent severing of the cause, future non-arising, and the natural dissolution of present formations once past karmic cause is exhausted, is the truth of cessation established on the strength of nirvana without residue. Moreover, the right view capable of realising ultimate truth, together with every noble path led by that right view, is called the truth of the path. Moreover, wishing that suffering be comprehended, origination permanently severed, cessation directly realised, and the path cultivated, the marks of the noble truths are briefly established. And so that the coarse marks of the truth of suffering serve as a foundation for gradually entering its subtle marks, the various sufferings beginning with birth are set forth first, and only afterwards is the suffering of the five clinging-aggregates shown. Moreover, according to differences in conduct, three kinds of person are established: lower, middling, and superior. One without self-benefiting or other-benefiting conduct is a lower person; one with either self-benefiting or other-benefiting conduct alone is a middling person; one with both self-benefiting and other-benefiting conduct is a superior person.

blocks.text: The king's sūtra ends: "follow this, and you are called a Dharma king". Then a new sūtra: the eight kinds of suffering, explained mark by mark.
Faults avoided, virtues cultivated, decline avoided, skilful means studied. Master Cháng Bǎi: the eight sufferings, in brief, are the suffering of the five clinging-aggregates.

Master Cháng Bǎi: ageing, sickness, death, separation from the loved, and meeting the hated all rest on the aggregates; without their arising there would be none. Not by one's own wish one parts from the aggregates one loves.

subs.head: A lamp nearly out of oil

blocks.text: Ageing: decline of appearance, vigour, faculties, enjoyment, and lifespan. Sickness: Master Cháng Bǎi, one must force oneself to take bitter medicine.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the most painful thing at death is that one's own body must be given up. Parted from a loved one, one longs for their good points, and the mind burns.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the coarse heaviness of affliction's seeds runs through all feelings. Neutral feeling is like an abscess with neither heat nor cold touching it; still an abscess. Seeing this, sages do not delight even in the peak of existence.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha taught craving as origin because it most clearly draws results. With remainder, the cause of suffering is ended and the result remains; without remainder, both are gone. One who benefits only one side is middling; both together, superior.
"A lamp whose oil is nearly spent." Ageing described without fear, simply as what it is.

quiz.q: In concluding, what does the Blessed One urge about gateways of decline and of skilful means?
options: decline should be studied to understand it, while skilful means need only be admired
both should be avoided
the gateways of decline should be avoided, and those of skilful means studied and practised
both should be practised
quiz.why: The conclusion assigns a verb to each of the six. Master Cháng Bǎi: faults avoided, virtues cultivated, decline avoided, skilful means studied, beloved qualities aspired to, and what draws them forth actually practised. Only the fifth is mere aspiration.

quiz.q: Why is birth called the basis of many sufferings, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the pressure of the birth canal is life's greatest pain, which outweighs all later suffering
because the parents suffer
ageing, sickness, death, and the rest all depend on the aggregates, and without birth they would not exist
only birth in bad destinies is painful
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ageing, sickness, death, separation from the loved, meeting the hated, and not getting what one seeks all rest on the aggregates; without their arising these would not occur, and so birth is their basis.

quiz.q: Which is not among the five areas of decline in ageing?
options: decline of appearance and vigour
decline of faculties and enjoyment
decline of wealth
decline of lifespan
quiz.why: The five are appearance, vigour, faculties, enjoyment, and lifespan. Wealth appears under death's suffering as something one parts from. Master Cháng Bǎi: lifespan's decline is harder still, for each day passed is one less.

quiz.q: Among death's five marks, which does Master Cháng Bǎi call most painful?
options: parting from wealth, since a lifetime's savings cannot be carried along
parting from friends
parting from family
parting from one's beloved body, which must immediately be given up
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the most painful thing at death is that one's own body must at once be given up. §19's English announces five marks but lists three, since the fourth and fifth open §20, so the two sections must be read together.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the burning of mind in parting from the loved?
options: the body gets a fever after parting, another way of saying bodily distress
resenting the other's leaving
regretting one's own words
on parting one recalls and longs for all the other's good qualities, and the mind burns greatly with distress
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when parted from a loved one, one longs for that person's many good points, and for this reason the mind burns with great distress. Bodily distress is the separate third mark, so the fourth lies in the mind.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the suffering of formations pervading the three feelings?
options: the coarse-heaviness of affliction seeds pervades pleasant, painful, and neutral feeling, and on this the nature of formations' suffering is set up
formations' suffering exists only in neutral feeling, each of the three sufferings having one feeling alone
it exists only above the form realm
it simply means bodily pain
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the coarse-heaviness of affliction seeds runs through all pleasant, painful, and neutral feelings, and on this basis the nature of formations' suffering is established. He notes that this differs from the treatment in fascicle 52.

quiz.q: In the simile of the hot abscess, what does each feeling correspond to?
options: pleasant is the abscess itself, painful the cool touch, and neutral the ash, being easily ignored
all three are like falling ash
all three are like the cool touch
pleasant is the cool touch, painful is falling hot ash, and neutral is the abscess's own suffering apart from both
quiz.why: The abscess itself stands for coarse-heaviness. Master Cháng Bǎi: with neither pain nor pleasure, neutral feeling is like being free of cool and hot touches, and the abscess's own suffering then shows clearly. Note that the simile's setup is missing from the English.

quiz.q: Having observed with noble wisdom, how do noble ones regard the aggregates of the peak of existence?
options: they do not wish for it, let alone the wretched hells
they still wish for it as the stillest state, shunning only the bad destinies
they take it to be nirvana
only stream-enterers refuse it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing suffering in formations, sages do not delight even in the peak of existence, the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, because it too is impermanent. If the highest existence is rejected, how much more the hells.

quiz.q: Why do the sutras show only craving as origination, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: only craving is origination, the sutra overruling the treatise's prior statement
they speak by the affliction most clearly drawing forth results; by characteristic, both karma and affliction are origination
craving is hardest to grasp
the sutra text has gaps
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha, going by the affliction that most clearly attracts results, taught only craving as origination; by the principle of characteristics, all karma and affliction producing future existence are origination. Two views, not a conflict.

quiz.q: How do the cessations established on nirvana with and without residue differ?
options: in the first, affliction's coarse-heaviness ends; in the second, causes end and present formations fade away of themselves
the first is for ordinary people, the second for sages, since the first keeps afflictions
first in the desire realm, second in the form realm
they are entirely the same
quiz.why: With residue, the cause of suffering is ended while the result remains. Without residue, Master Cháng Bǎi says, both the cause and the result of suffering are completely ended. Both belong to those who have ended afflictions, so the difference lies in the remaining fruit.

quiz.q: Among the three persons by conduct, how is the middling person defined?
options: having either self-benefiting or other-benefiting conduct alone
having both kinds of conduct, though not yet perfectly, ranking just below the superior
having neither kind of conduct
meditating but never giving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one who can benefit only one side, oneself or others but not both, is a middling person. Both together make a superior person, and neither a lower person. The measure is breadth of conduct, not degree.
